The Sotogrande Polo Final 2036 is one of the Costa del Sol’s most prestigious sporting events, drawing international crowds to the Santa María Polo Club. Watching from the water offers a unique vantage point, combining the match with the Mediterranean breeze. A marbella boat rental sotogrande polo final 2036 lets you anchor just offshore, with all-inclusive service from Puerto Banús. Our fleet departs from the marina, and every charter includes a skipper, drinks, snacks, and insurance – no hidden fees.

Why Watch the Polo Final from a Boat?

The Santa María Polo Club’s main field runs directly along the coastline. By anchoring a few metres offshore, you get an uninterrupted view of the chukkas while enjoying the comfort of your own vessel. There’s no need to jostle for a spot on the beach or pay for expensive hospitality tents. On a boat, you control the music, the shade, and the drinks. Plus, you can take a dip between chukkas – the water temperature in August averages 24 °C.

Our Fleet for the 2036 Final

We offer boats ranging from 5 to 12 passengers, all departing from Puerto Banús. Here’s a quick overview:

  • Tier A – Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) & Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax): €749/2h → €2,299/8h. All inclusive.
  • Tier B – Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) & Mangusta 80 Grey (24m, 12 pax): €4,719 minimum 4h, with free jet ski.

All vessels include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, and Spanish IVA (21%). For the full fleet list, visit our [main page](/).

How to Get There

All charters depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella’s iconic marina. The cruise to Sotogrande takes 15–20 minutes, depending on your boat’s speed. You’ll pass the Golden Mile, Cabopino, and the dunes of Artola before reaching the polo club’s bay. Parking at Puerto Banús is available (paid), and taxis from Sotogrande cost around €30–40.

What to Expect on the Day

The 2036 final is expected in mid-August, with the match starting late afternoon (around 17:00). We recommend departing Puerto Banús by 15:30 to allow time to anchor and settle. Your skipper will position the boat for the best view. Bring sunscreen, hats, and swimwear – the sun is strong, and you’ll likely want to cool off between chukkas. Our standard drinks package covers beer, wine, cava, and soft drinks; you’re welcome to bring your own food.

Booking Tips for the 2036 Final

Demand for boats during the Sotogrande Polo Final is high. We advise booking 3–4 months in advance, especially for the larger vessels like the Mangusta 80 or Ferretti 94. Tier A boats are more budget-friendly and still offer excellent views. For groups of 10–12, the Azimut 58 Flybridge or Lagoon 380 are popular choices. To secure your preferred boat, message us on WhatsApp with your date, group size, and preferred duration. We’ll confirm availability and send a quote.

If you need a specific vessel not listed in our tiers – such as the Pershing 46 (14m, 10 pax), Fairline Targa 12m (12m, 10 pax), or the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) – just ask. For the best experience, let us know if you’d like to add a jet ski (already free on Tier B) or a custom catering menu.
